tools.name: vault
tools.description: 📁 File operations - list, read, create, update, delete, search, fragments, move, rename, copy, split, combine, concatenate. Search supports: operators (file:, path:, content:, tag:), OR/AND, "quoted phrases", <CHEMIN_PRIVE>`graph.neighbors` to reach what search cannot rank.

raw.description: Return raw JSON instead of formatted markdown (use when you need complete metadata or structured data for processing)

path.description: File path relative to vault root

query.description: Search query - supports operators (file:, path:, content:, tag:), OR/AND, "quoted phrases", /regex/

ranked.description: Use TF-IDF relevance scoring (default: auto-detected based on query type)

searchStrategy.description: Search strategy: auto (detect from query), filename (names only), content (full-text), combined (both)

includeSnippets.description: Extract contextual snippets around matches (default: true)

page.description: Page number for paginated results (list/search; also large-file read — see returnFullFile)

strategy.description: Fragment retrieval strategy (default: auto). None of these are embedding/vector search — all match words, not meaning. auto: pick per query. adaptive: term-frequency ranked passages. proximity: passages where the query terms appear close together. structure: passages cut on the document's own structure (headings, paragraphs) with surrounding context kept. "semantic" is a deprecated alias of "structure" — it never meant vector similarity, and is retained only for compatibility.

maxFragments.description: Maximum number of fragments to return (default: 5)

returnFullFile.description: read: force the ENTIRE file verbatim regardless of size (explicit large-context override). Default read already returns the whole file verbatim when it fits the size budget; large files return a verbatim page 1 with absolute line bookends (use page=N to continue, or query/strategy/maxFragments for fragments).

includeContent.description: Include file content in search results (slower but more thorough)

destination.description: Destination path for move/copy/combine operations. For combine: omit to return the combined content inline without writing a file

newName.description: New filename for rename operation (without path). If the extension is omitted, the source file's extension is preserved (renaming "note.md" to "renamed" yields "renamed.md")

overwrite.description: Whether to overwrite if destination exists (default: false)

splitBy.description: Split strategy: heading (by markdown headings), delimiter (by custom string), lines (by line count), size (by character count)

linesPerFile.description: Number of lines per file for lines strategy (default: 100)

maxSize.description: Max characters per file for size strategy (default: 10000)

outputDirectory.description: Directory for output files (defaults to source directory)

paths.description: Array of file paths to combine

includeFilenames.description: Include source filenames as headers (default: false)

mode.description: Concatenation mode: append to path1, prepend to path1, or create new file

tools.description: ✏️ Edit files - window: find/replace with fuzzy matching, append: add to end, patch: modify headings/blocks/frontmatter, at_line: insert at line number, from_buffer: reuse previous window content

targetType.description: Structure to target: heading (use :: for nesting), block (by ID), or frontmatter (field name)

tools.name: graph
tools.description: 🕸️ Graph navigation — follow the vault's own links. Use this to EXPAND from a note you already found rather than running another search: search ranks by term frequency, so it cannot reach a note that covers the topic in different words, but a link to it usually exists. BLIND SPOT (the mirror of search's): traversal only reaches what someone actually linked. A note can be genuinely relevant and simply unlinked — no amount of traversal will find it. So the two are complements, not substitutes: scan broadly with `vault.search` to catch the unlinked, then follow links from the hits to catch the differently-worded. Trust neither alone. Actions — neighbors: immediate links of a note (start here); traverse: multi-hop exploration; search-traverse: scan-and-follow in one call, but it returns SNIPPETS per node and prunes on scoreThreshold, so use it to discover WHICH notes matter, then read them — do not treat its snippets as the whole argument; path: how two notes connect; backlinks/forwardlinks: directional links (backlinks are how you find what depends on a note — its own text does not know); statistics: link counts (call with no sourcePath for vault-wide density); tag-analysis/shared-tags: tag structure.

raw.description: Return raw JSON instead of formatted markdown (use when you need complete metadata or structured data for processing)

sourcePath.description: Starting file path for graph operations

targetPath.description: Target file path (for path finding operations)

maxNodes.description: Maximum number of nodes to return (default: 50)

includeUnresolved.description: Include unresolved links in the results

followForwardLinks.description: Follow forward links during traversal (default: true)

fileFilter.description: Regex pattern to filter file names

tagFilter.description: Only include files with these tags

folderFilter.description: Only include files in this folder

startPath.description: Starting document path for search traversal

searchQuery.description: Search query to apply at each node (for search-traverse)

maxSnippetsPerNode.description: Maximum snippets to extract per node (default: 2)

scoreThreshold.description: Minimum score threshold for including nodes (0-1, default: 0.5)

filePattern.description: Filter traversal to files matching this pattern

tagWeight.description: Weight factor for tag connections (0-1, default: 0.8)

tools.name: bases
tools.description: 🗃️ Bases operations - list: show all .base files, read: get YAML config, create: new base with views/filters/formulas, query: execute filters on vault notes, view: get table/card view data, evaluate: test formulas, export: CSV/JSON/Markdown. Bases use YAML format with expression-based filters like status == "active" and file.hasTag("project")

raw.description: Return raw JSON instead of formatted markdown (use when you need complete metadata or structured data for processing)

config.description: Base configuration object with name, source, properties, and views

viewName.description: Name of the view to retrieve

filters.description: Array of filter objects with property, operator, and value

sort.description: Sort options with property and order (asc/desc)

pagination.description: Pagination options with page and pageSize

properties.description: Specific properties to include in results

basePath.description: Path to the base for template generation

template.description: Template configuration with name, folder, properties, and contentTemplate
